svg.text: Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'ground'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: G01: BAT12.neg -> GND_STAR.G - Same size as the main feed
G02: DCDC.out_neg -> GND_STAR.G
G03: TVS.A -> GND_STAR.G
G04: PI_BUCK.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G05: PI5.GND -> PI_BUCK.GND
G06: PICO_BUCK.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G07: PICO.GND -> PICO_BUCK.GND - All control box boards share the Pico ground
G08: SCREEN_PSU.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G09: SCREEN.GND -> SCREEN_PSU.GND
G10: AMP.GND -> GND_STAR.G - Same size as the feed
G24: GLOVE_USB.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G11: MOSFET.GND -> GND_STAR.G - Carries the current of all 8 lights on the board (about 30 A with everything on)
G15: BTS9.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G33: BEACON.GND -> GND_STAR.G - Beacon earth, or a good chassis earth on the roll cage
G16: BTS4.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G31: BTS5.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G32: BTS6.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G25: BTS7.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G26: BTS8.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G27: HEAD_L.GND -> GND_STAR.G - Stock earth, keep it if it's good
G28: HEAD_R.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G29: TAIL_L.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G30: TAIL_R.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G12: BTS1.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G13: BTS2.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G14: BTS3.B- -> GND_STAR.G
G17: WINCH_SOL.GND -> BAT12.neg - Winch return straight to the battery, cable from the winch kit
G37: RELAYS.GND -> PICO_BUCK.GND - Relay coil return (JD-VCC side)
G38: RELAYS2.GND -> PICO_BUCK.GND
G39: MCP1.GND -> PICO.GND - Logic ground. Without it the board has no ground and never answers on I2C
G40: MCP2.GND -> PICO.GND
G41: ADS1.GND -> PICO.GND - Also the diff pot's low end (D10)
G42: PCA.GND -> PICO.GND
G43: PICO_CAN.GND -> PICO.GND
G44: EPS_CAN.GND -> PICO.GND
G45: OPTO.GND -> PICO.GND - 3.3 V side only. COM12 (12 V side) stays on the chassis ground (G19), so the opto still isolates
G46: BTS1.GND -> PICO.GND - BTS7960 logic header ground, so the Pico's PWM has a reference. B- carries the load current
G47: BTS2.GND -> PICO.GND
G48: BTS3.GND -> PICO.GND
G49: BTS4.GND -> PICO.GND
G50: BTS5.GND -> PICO.GND
G51: BTS6.GND -> PICO.GND
G52: BTS7.GND -> PICO.GND
G53: BTS8.GND -> PICO.GND
G54: BTS9.GND -> PICO.GND
G55: PI_CAN.GND -> PI5.GND - Header ground pin, with the CAN board's other leads
G56: RC_CAN.GND -> RC_PICO.GND
G57: RC_LVL.GND -> RC_PICO.GND
G58: RC_DAC.GND -> RC_PICO.GND
G59: RC_ADC.GND -> RC_PICO.GND
G60: RC_REL.GND -> RC_PICO.GND
G19: OPTO.COM12 -> GND_STAR.G - 12 V side ground of the opto board
G20: TRAILER.P3_EARTH -> GND_STAR.G
G21: TCAM_PLUG.GND -> GND_STAR.G
G22: EPS_ECU.GND -> BAT12.neg
G23: CAM_TRAILER.GND -> TCAM_PLUG.GND - Earth the camera at the hitch, not through the 7-pin earth
G34: CAM_REAR.GND -> GND_STAR.G - Or a good chassis earth near the camera
G36: MODEM_4G.G -> PI5.GND - Ground with the UART leads
GND_STAR: Ground point (star) - One solid chassis ground near the fuse block. Every 12 V ground goes here
RC_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (RC box, main bus) - Same 3.3 V-converted board as the control box (TJA1050 swapped for SN65HVD230). A short stub off the main bus inside the control box, no terminator
BAT12: 12 V aux battery - Kept after the conversion. Charged by the DC-DC
DCDC: DC-DC converter 72 V to 12 V - Charges the 12 V battery. Rating TBC; it decides how long winch + steering can run
TVS: 1.5KE18A TVS diode - Clamps spikes on the dash rail

PI_BUCK: Potted 5 V 10 A buck (12/24 V in) - Sealed car-type 12/24 V to 5 V 10 A (50 W) buck, input 8-35 V or wider. Feeds the Pi 5 (about 16 W with the AI HAT+ 2) and the 4G board (2 A peaks), so about 30 W worst case of its 50 W. Wide input rides out spikes the Mini560 (20 V max) couldn't
g.text: Potted 5 V 10 A buck (12/24 V in)

g.title: PICO_BUCK: 5 V 5 A buck (Sam's, control box)

SCREEN_PSU: Screen 12 V supply - LTC3780 buck-boost board (5-32 V in, set to 12.0 V, 80 W) in the Pi box. Keeps the screen on a steady 12 V while the battery swings 11-14.4 V. No reverse-polarity protection, so it sits after the fuse. Skip it if the screen's own board says 9-36 V in

AMP: 4-ch class D amp (AliExpress, 4 x 63 W RMS at 4 ohm) - Sam's pick. 4 x 63 W RMS at 4 ohm, or 2 x 200 W RMS bridged at 4 ohm; built-in 90 Hz high and low pass; 8-16 V; up to 33 A flat out (16.5 A on music); 145 x 100 x 45 mm. Channels 1 and 2 drive the Kenwoods (set the HPF on). Channels 3 and 4 bridged (200 W at 4 ohm) drive the Kicker KM104 sub (LPF on, gain set so it stays under the sub's 150 W RMS)

GLOVE_USB: Glove box USB-C charger (RC phone) - 12 V to USB-C PD socket for the phone that lives in the glove box (docs/rc-beach-launch.md 4b). Fed from the accessory relay so it's off with the key off

MOSFET: 8-ch isolated MOSFET board (low side, all 8 used) - Sam's board: 8-channel opto-isolated MOSFET driver, DC 3.7-27 V, 10 A per channel, PWM input 3-20 V, 0-20 kHz. 1-4 front bars, 5 cabin bar, 6 trailer bar, 7-8 rear floods. Low side switching, so each light's + comes from its fuse and its - goes to an OUT pin
BTS9: BTS7960 9 (roof beacon amber / white) - Two-colour beacons usually share one earth wire, so the colours are switched on the + side like the stock lamps: RPWM amber, LPWM white

BEACON: Roof beacon (amber + white LED, steady-on) - Sam's amber + white LED beacon (bought 18 Nov). Each colour stays on steady and the Pico flashes them at 3 Hz (NZ Vehicle Lighting Rule 11.1(2): 2 to 4 Hz), amber and white taking turns. White only when stopped: on the road only red or amber may show to the rear. Fits Sam's existing hole on the roof

BTS4: BTS7960 4 (left headlight low / high) - Used as two high-side switches, not a motor bridge. VCC from the Pico 3.3 V like BTS1-3. EN (R_EN + L_EN) from PCA9685 PWM15 with a 10k to ground, so the lamps stay off until the Pico is running
BTS5: BTS7960 5 (right headlight low / high)
BTS6: BTS7960 6 (left tail / brake)
BTS7: BTS7960 7 (right tail / brake)
BTS8: BTS7960 8 (trailer tail / stop)
HEAD_L: Left headlight (stock, 12 V 35/35 W) - Dual filament bulb, low and high, one shared earth (Kawasaki 2013 Teryx 750 owner's manual: headlight 12 V 35/35 W x 2)
HEAD_R: Right headlight (stock, 12 V 35/35 W)
TAIL_L: Left tail / brake light (stock, 12 V 8/27 W) - Dual filament bulb, 8 W tail and 27 W brake, one shared earth (owner's manual: tail/brake light 12 V 8/27 W x 2)
TAIL_R: Right tail / brake light (stock, 12 V 8/27 W)
BTS1: BTS7960 1 (front diff)
BTS2: BTS7960 2 (2WD/4WD)
BTS3: BTS7960 3 (tray)
OPTO: 8-ch opto board (PC817, 12 V in) - All 8 channels used. OUT8 (trailer) goes to MCP2 B0. A second 8-ch board (AliExpress cart) gives spare inputs on MCP2 B1-B6 (B7 is output only)
TRAILER: 7-pin flat trailer socket (Narva 82043BL, reed switch)

TCAM_PLUG: Trailer EU 7-pin round plug (camera + light bar, Sam's) - Sam's EU round 7-pin, next to the flat NZ/AU 7-pin for the main trailer lights, so they can't be mixed up. NOT wired to the EU light standard. 1 cam +12 V, 2 video, 3 cam ground, 4 video shield, 5 light bar +12 V, 6 light bar - (switched), 7 spare. Light bar on 1.5 mm² (pins are good for 10 A+). Spring cap on the socket and dielectric grease on the pins

CAM_REAR: Rear camera (200 degree, Sam's) - Sam thinks it's AHD. Set to CVBS/PAL mode, soldered shielded video lead to the analogue-to-ribbon board. Rear or trailer is picked in software when the trailer plug is in. 12 V from the accessory relay (relay 7) through its own 2 A inline fuse

RC_PICO: RC box Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (spare from the 5-pack) - Second Pico, only for RC. Drives the steering by faking the torque sensor. If it stops or loses power the changeover relay drops and the real torque sensor is back. Pins TBC in the RC firmware; these are a starting point

WINCH_SOL: XBull solenoid box - The remote socket's in and out lines are cut from the coils inside the box and rejoined through their own diodes (WN21, WN22), like the hand switches. Then the in.winch_remote tap sees only the remote, not the Pico's own relays 4-5 driving the coils (found by the system sim, 23 Nov: tapped at the coil, the Pico would stop its own winch pull)

EPS_ECU: Toyota Aqua EPS ECU (89650-52B51) - Owned with its power plug (B+, GND). Still need the signal plug (IG, CANH, CANL). Pin numbers TBC: Toyota's RAV4 EPS ECU has IG, CANH, CANL on one plug and PIG, PGND on the other
PI5: Raspberry Pi 5 8GB - The 40-pin header and the PCIe port are kept for the AI HAT+ 2. CAN module wires go to header pins that come up through the HAT
PICO: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 - Talks to the Pi over CAN only. No USB lead to the Pi; reflash with a laptop on its own USB port in the workshop
SCREEN: 10.1 in touch screen - 1280x800, HDMI + USB touch, 3.5 mm audio in

RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
RELAYS2: 16-ch relay board, channels 9-16 (2 used, 6 spare) - Same board as RELAYS. Relay 9 steering enable, relay 10 drive lock (uses the NC contact)
RC_LVL: I2C level shifter, 4-ch BSS138 (3.3 V to 5 V) - The DAC and ADC run on 5 V so they can reach the torque sensor's range (up to about 3.5 V). The Pico's I2C is 3.3 V, so it goes through this

RC_DAC: MCP4728 4-ch 12-bit DAC (0x60) - VOUTA = fake TRQ1, VOUTB = fake TRQ2 (a mirrored pair about the centre, trq_volts() in teryx/rc_mode.py). C and D spare (throttle wiper later). VDD 5 V, so 0-5 V out

RC_ADC: ADS1115 ADC (third one, 0x48 on the RC box's own I2C) - Reads back what actually reaches the ECU (A0 TRQ1, A1 TRQ2) and the steering angle (A2). If TRQ1/TRQ2 stop mirroring, the RC box drops the relay. VDD 5 V so it can read up to 5 V

RC_REL: DPDT signal relay module, 5 V coil, gold contacts - Off (NC) = the real torque sensor goes to the ECU. On (NO) = the DAC does. Not the 16-ch board: its 10 A silver contacts aren't made for tiny sensor currents. The coil only gets power from the RC box, so anything that stops the RC box hands the steering back
CAM_TRAILER: Trailer camera (12 V AHD)
MCP1: MCP23017 I/O expander (0x20)

MCP2: Second MCP23017 (0x21) - Steering enable and drive lock relays, and the trailer input on B0. Newer MCP23017 chips say GPA7/GPB7 are outputs only (Microchip datasheet rev D on), so the trailer input moved here off MCP1 B7
ADS1: ADS1115 ADC (0x48) - ALERT pin left free so GP22 can be the steering CAN chip select (read "ready" over I2C)

PCA: PCA9685 16-ch PWM board (0x40) - Every light that isn't a front bar or the cabin bar dims through this (docs/lights.md). Wires soldered straight to the pads, no header pins. VCC 3.3 V so the outputs are 3.3 V, which the MOSFET boards (3-20 V input) and the BTS7960s (3.3 V logic like BTS1-3) take. Leave V+ (servo power) empty. OE tied low on the board. PWM0 trailer bar, 1-10 stock lights on BTS7960 4-8, 11-12 rear floods, 13-14 beacon amber / white on BTS7960 9, 15 BTS7960 enable. All outputs are off at power-up

PICO_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (control box) - Blue AliExpress MCP2515 board (8 MHz crystal) with its 5 V TJA1050 swapped for a 3.3 V SN65HVD230 (same pins), so the whole board runs on 3.3 V. Never fit one with the TJA1050 still on: it puts 5 V on the Pico pins
EPS_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (steering bus) - Own 500 kbit/s bus to the steering ECU. INT not wired, the Pico polls it for the ECU's replies
PI_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (Pi) - Blue MCP2515 board with the SN65HVD230 swap (as the control box one), on the Pi box wall. 8 MHz crystal: pi-setup.sh default

MODEM_4G: SIMCom A7670SA 4G board - 6-pin header S G V K T R G. V takes 5-10 V: a soldered lead from the Pi buck (5 V). NEVER raw 12 V (10 V max, and the car runs 14.4 V with spikes). K is tied to ground on the board, so it starts by itself. T/R are 115200 baud TTL to the Pi's GPIO 15/14; measure T before connecting (3.3 V ok, else BSS138). Micro USB also on board. Its GNSS (FASE version, u.FL GPS socket on Sam's board) is the dash GPS too, so there is no separate USB GPS. Check on arrival that it gets a fix with the SIM out / 4G off. No USB: it's on the header pins (soldered leads), so texts, GPS and slow data only, no live video over 4G
